claims.claim: **Treat IV fluid as a prescribed medication; use the enteral route whenever possible.** This guidance applies from 1 month to 18 years.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** sodium under 135 or over 145 mmol/L, or changing by more than 0.5 mmol/L/hr — notify a senior clinician; short gut or major GI pathology; **resuscitation over 20 mL/kg.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weigh at the start and at least daily** — serial weights are the most reliable guide to fluid status. Record intake and losses with at least 12-hourly subtotals.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check electrolytes and glucose before starting, and at least every 24 hours** while running more than 50% maintenance; recheck at 4–6 hours in sicker children or with large losses or abnormal electrolytes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Shock: 10–20 mL/kg sodium chloride 0.9% as fast as possible, reassess after each bolus, repeat 10–20 mL/kg as needed.** Senior clinician at ≥20 mL/kg; **consider inotropes at ≥40 mL/kg.** Bolus volumes are not counted in later calculations.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Trauma: packed red cells 10 mL/kg first-line.** Plasma-Lyte 148, Hartmann's or albumin only on senior advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never give a glucose-containing fluid as a shock bolus.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintenance: sodium chloride 0.9% with glucose 5% (± potassium)** in most situations; include glucose (usually 5%) for most children, especially nil by mouth.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatives:** Plasma-Lyte 148 with glucose 5% (5 mmol/L potassium, less chloride) for hyperchloraemia and acidosis. Hartmann's with glucose 5% is rarely used and **is incompatible with some drugs, e.g. ceftriaxone.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Potassium chloride 20 mmol/L**, premixed with sodium chloride 0.9% and glucose 5%, once electrolytes and renal function are known.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Glucose 15–20%** only on senior advice, ideally centrally; **over 20%** only in intensive care.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypotonic fluids (e.g. sodium chloride 0.45%) are not for routine use** — only with a senior clinician or in intensive care; they may cause hyponatraemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Full maintenance (well children only):** 3–10 kg: 100 mL/kg/day (4 mL/kg/hr); 10–20 kg: 1000 + 50 × (weight − 10) mL/day [40 + 2 × (weight − 10) mL/hr]; 20–60 kg: 1500 + 20 × (weight − 20) mL/day [60 + 1 × (weight − 20) mL/hr]; over 60 kg: normal maximum 2400 mL/day (100 mL/hr). Consider ideal body weight; adjust for all unwell children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants: base the IV prescription on water requirement (100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg)**, not the 150–180 mL/kg/day enteral milk volume.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use 2/3 maintenance in most unwell children unless dehydrated** — high ADH risks water overload and hyponatraemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Further restriction may be needed (seek senior advice)** in acute CNS conditions, pulmonary conditions including bronchiolitis and ventilation, post-operatively and after trauma.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Replace at most 5% deficit over 24 hours (on top of maintenance), then reassess.** Over 5% dehydrated — e.g. 10% — replace 5% in the first 24 hours and 5% in the next 24.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinician estimates of % dehydration are unreliable** — use a constant rate on premorbid weight and adjust only the duration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dehydrated child, maintenance + 5% deficit over 24 hours:** under 4 kg — consult a senior clinician · 5 kg 30 · 10 kg 60 · 20 kg 100 · 30 kg 130 · 40 kg 160 · 50 kg 190 mL/hr.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Deranged electrolytes:** consult a senior clinician and consider slower deficit replacement.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Replace significant ongoing losses** by the previous hour or 4-hour period (e.g. 200 mL over 4 hours → 50 mL/hr for the next 4), GI losses usually with **0.9% sodium chloride plus 20 mmol/L potassium chloride**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use a burette in small children; set pumps to an hourly volume and check it each hour.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for severe electrolyte or glucose abnormalities, or **shock needing ≥40 mL/kg of boluses.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intravenous fluids' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intravenous_fluids/, retrieved 2026-09-23
